name: Judas Barsabbas
title: Prophet and messenger from Jerusalem
summary: Judas Barsabbas was a leading man among the believers in Jerusalem who was chosen together with Silas to accompany Paul and Barnabas back to Antioch. He brought the important letter from the apostolic council in Jerusalem which established that Gentile Christians did not need to follow the entire Mosaic Law. He served as a prophet and encouraged the church with his words.

keyEvents.title: Chosen as messenger
keyEvents.description: Judas Barsabbas was chosen together with Silas by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem to accompany Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with the letter from the apostolic council.

keyEvents.title: Described as a leading man
keyEvents.description: The Acts of the Apostles describes Judas Barsabbas as a leading man among the brothers in Jerusalem, which shows his standing in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Delivering the Apostles' Council Letter
keyEvents.description: Judas and Silas delivered the important letter from Jerusalem that freed Gentile Christians from circumcision and most of the Mosaic Law.

keyEvents.title: Prophetic Ministry in Antioch
keyEvents.description: As prophets, Judas and Silas encouraged and strengthened the believers in Antioch with many words, and urged the congregation in their faith.

keyEvents.title: Sent Back with Peace
keyEvents.description: After a time in Antioch, Judas was sent back to Jerusalem with a greeting of peace from the brothers there.
